description: Hi! I'm Zarar, a student developer and motion graphics artist from Pakistan. Team Rover Stories will tell the stories of NASA's rovers, landers and probes left on the Moon, Mars and in deep space, through animation, for school kids.
summary: Rover Stories is a 2-minute animated film for school kids in which NASA's forgotten machines tell their own stories in first person. Kids meet the Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle on the Moon, the Opportunity rover on Mars and Voyager 1 in deep space. Each machine explains what it was, why it was sent, and the real science it made possible: the Genesis Rock, the hematite "blueberries" that showed Mars once had water, volcanoes on Io, the Pale Blue Dot photo and reaching interstellar space. Kids usually only hear about active missions, while the history of these machines is buried in dense technical websites. A short, emotional story with real NASA images, captions and fact badges makes that history easy to watch in a classroom or at home, and helps kids feel a personal connection to these robotic explorers.
details: WHAT IT DOES: Rover Stories is a short animated film (1 min 56 sec) for school kids aged about 8-14. Three NASA machines that were left behind tell their own stories in first person: the Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle (Moon, 1971), the Opportunity rover (Mars, 2004-2018) and Voyager 1 (deep space, 1977-today). Every scene connects the engineering to the science: the Moon buggy let astronauts travel farther and collect the Genesis Rock; Opportunity was planned for 90 days but drove more than 45 km and found hematite 'blueberries' that formed in water; Voyager 1 discovered volcanoes on Io, took the Pale Blue Dot photo and reached interstellar space in 2012. BENEFITS AND IMPACT: Kids usually only hear about active missions. A story told by the machines themselves is emotional and easy to remember, and teachers can show it in class. Next steps: more episodes (Spirit, Ingenuity, Viking, Pioneer 10), an Urdu version for kids in Pakistan, and an interactive map of 'ghost rovers'. HOW WE BUILT IT: Real images from the NASA Image and Video Library. The script was written and fact-checked against NASA mission facts. Narration uses ElevenLabs AI text-to-speech with stock voices (a different voice for each machine). The animation is built in code with Remotion (React and TypeScript): word-level timings from the voice drive the captions and the animated fact badges, with Ken Burns camera moves and title animations. Videos are hosted on YouTube, code on GitHub. CREATIVITY: The machines are the narrators, so kids feel a personal connection. Full film: https://youtu.be/NByJu1hZeuk Slides: https://github.com/Zaari786/rover-stories/blob/main/slides/Rover-Stories-Slides.pdf USE OF AI: Claude Code (Anthropic) helped write the script and the animation code; ElevenLabs generated the narration voices (credited in the video and descriptions). Images are real NASA photos, not AI-generated. I directed the story, chose the machines and style, and reviewed every scene.
